answers.answer: Yes. For Career Ladder teachers, eligible teachers move vertically to the next step annually, but those with an unsatisfactory rating are not eligible to advance. Advanced Study and Longevity increments do not apply in the Career Ladder salary schedule. For non-Career Ladder teachers, increments for Steps 1-9 receive increases at each step annually over the five-year agreement, with amounts in the salary schedules. Teachers at the top step receive a $1,500 increase each year, plus a $1,000 bonus if the District attains AYP. Teachers at the top of the salary schedule who participate in and are selected for the limited pilot VIEW Pay Program relinquish the negotiated increment at the top of the salary schedule, and 40% of the bonus rolls to the base salary schedule annually. Movement from step 9 to step 10a and then to 10b requires remaining at 10a for six months of the work-year before moving to 10b; for example, if a teacher has been at step 10a for three working months when the current contract ends, they have only three working months remaining before moving to step 10b in the new contract.

answers.answer: Yes. The document includes the VIEW (Voluntary Incentive Earnings at Work) Pay Program, a voluntary pilot performance pay plan for current teachers in positions requiring certification and employed as of June 30, 2010. Eligible teachers in all subject areas may volunteer. Criteria require demonstrating the ability to grow student achievement, measured via a value-added model for core subjects or Student Learning Outcomes designated by a design team for non-core subjects. The bonus ranges up to a maximum of $8,000 per volunteer annually. The pilot caps increase annually: 75 teachers in 2011-12, 125 in 2012-13, 175 in 2013-14, and 225 in 2014-15. If more teachers volunteer than the cap, a random selection will occur. Teachers at the top of the salary schedule who participate relinquish their negotiated increment, with 40% of the bonus rolling to their base salary annually; tenured teachers on internal steps continue step advancement with no portion of the bonus rolling. At the conclusion of the pilot, participating teachers may choose to continue in the plan or return to the traditional salary schedule.
answers.evidence: If a teacher chooses to participate in the VIEW Pay Program, he/she must demonstrate the ability to grow student achievement. Teachers in all subject areas will be eligible to volunteer. For teachers who teach core subjects, a value-added model of calculating student achievement will be available to them. For those teachers who do not have such testing data available to them, Student Learning Outcomes will be designated by the VIEW Pay Program design team (composed of fourteen teachers and two administrators.) Student Learning Outcomes are defined as “explicit statements describing knowledge, skills, abilities, and attitudes that a student will be able to demonstrate at the end (or as a result) of his or her engagement in a particular lesson, course, or program.”

answers.answer: The provided passages only specify reduction-in-force procedures for certain career ladder and special category roles, not a general district-wide procedure. For Clinical Resident Instructors (CRIs), reductions in force occur by special category seniority within the CRI pool and by building seniority within the resident staff; if a more senior teacher is laid off due to this, they are placed in a full-time substitute or equivalent temporary position without a salary change or break in service. In the event of school closings, Career Ladder teachers are considered displaced but have first right to vacancies in their former Career Ladder role. Promise Readiness Corps (PRC) teachers face reductions in force within the PRC Corps or non-PRC staff at the high school, with system seniority applying to furloughs; PRC special category seniority applies within buildings only, not across schools, and began in the 2011-2012 school year, with teachers selected for 2012-13 receiving one year of credit for 2011-12.
